name: Pay It Off Faster
description: A loan or mortgage with overpayments: monthly interest rounded to the penny, a fix that ends and a recalculated payment, lump sums, a payment holiday and early repayment charges above the 10% allowance. When is it cleared, how much interest is paid and saved, and what do the charges come to? Checked against an exact month-by-month simulation.
hook: Overpay the mortgage: when is it gone, and what does it save?
author: Gauntlet Real-World Pack

cases.prompt:
I took out a car loan of £9,000 at 7.90% a year. My first payment is in January 2027 and I pay £281.62 a month. I want to add £60 a month on top, from the very first month.

THE RULES MY LENDER USES (and you must use)
- Every month, interest = the balance × the annual rate ÷ 12, rounded to the nearest penny (halves round up), and is added to the balance. Then the monthly payment is taken (or the whole balance, if that is less). Then any overpayment for that month is taken (never more than what is left).
- When the payment is recalculated at the start of a month, it becomes the fixed monthly payment that would clear the balance (before that month’s interest) over the months left in the original term at the new rate: payment = B × i ÷ (1 − (1 + i)^−n), with i = annual rate ÷ 1200 and n = months left including that month, rounded UP to the next penny. It then stays the same until the next recalculation.
- The months are counted from the first payment (month 1 = January 2027).

With the overpayments, in which month is the last payment made, how many monthly payments is that, how much interest is paid in total, and how much interest does that save compared with making no overpayments at all (same rates and recalculations, normal payments only)?
Answer in this JSON format (money in pounds to the penny; the month as YYYY-MM):
```json
{"clearedMonth": "YYYY-MM", "months": 0, "totalInterest": 0.00, "interestSaved": 0.00}
```
Give exactly one answer as a single JSON block. Do not offer alternatives: a reply that contains two different answers, or an answer that says "or", is marked wrong. You may explain your working before the JSON.
